hints: Resolve perpendicular to the plane to find the normal reaction: $R = mg\cos 20^\circ$.
Calculate the maximum friction force using $F = \mu R = 0.35(30\cos 20^\circ)$.
For the least force $P_{\text{min}}$, the particle is about to slip down the plane, so friction acts up the plane: $P_{\text{min}} + F = mg\sin 20^\circ$.
For the greatest force $P_{\text{max}}$, the particle is about to slip up the plane, so friction acts down the plane: $P_{\text{max}} = mg\sin 20^\circ + F$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane to find the normal contact reaction:
$$R = mg\cos 20^\circ = 3(10)\cos 20^\circ = 30\cos 20^\circ \approx 28.1908\text{ N}$$

Calculate the limiting frictional force:
$$F = \mu R = 0.35 \times 28.1908 \approx 9.8668\text{ N}$$
and evaluate the downhill component of weight:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg\sin 20^\circ = 30\sin 20^\circ \approx 10.2606\text{ N}$$

For the minimum value of $P$, the particle is on the point of slipping down the plane, so friction acts upwards:
$$P_{\text{min}} + F = mg\sin 20^\circ$$
$$P_{\text{min}} = 10.2606 - 9.8668 = 0.3938\text{ N} \approx 0.394\text{ N}$$

For the maximum value of $P$, the particle is on the point of sliding up the plane, so friction acts downwards:
$$P_{\text{max}} = mg\sin 20^\circ + F$$
$$P_{\text{max}} = 10.2606 + 9.8668 = 20.1274\text{ N} \approx 20.1\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the equilibrium condition perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$\Sigma F_{\perp} = 0 \implies R - mg\cos 20^\circ = 0$$
Substitute $m = 3\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R = 3 \times 10 \times \cos 20^\circ = 30\cos 20^\circ$$
$$\cos 20^\circ \approx 0.939693 \implies R = 30 \times 0.939693 = 28.1908\text{ N}$$

State the limiting friction formula:
$$F = \mu R$$
Substitute $\mu = 0.35$ and $R = 28.1908\text{ N}$:
$$F = 0.35 \times 28.1908 = 9.86678\text{ N}$$

Calculate the downhill component of weight:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg\sin 20^\circ = 30\sin 20^\circ$$
$$\sin 20^\circ \approx 0.342020 \implies W_{\parallel} = 30 \times 0.342020 = 10.26060\text{ N}$$

Determine the least force $P_{\text{min}}$ to prevent slipping down:
Here, impending motion is down the plane, so friction acts upwards along the slope:
$$P_{\text{min}} + F - W_{\parallel} = 0$$
$$P_{\text{min}} = W_{\parallel} - F = 10.26060 - 9.86678 = 0.39382\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.394\text{ N}$, as required.

Determine the greatest force $P_{\text{max}}$ before slipping up:
Here, impending motion is up the plane, so friction opposes upward motion and acts downwards along the slope:
$$P_{\text{max}} - F - W_{\parallel} = 0$$
$$P_{\text{max}} = W_{\parallel} + F = 10.26060 + 9.86678 = 20.12738\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $20.1\text{ N}$.
